Hi Irene / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here at Acme is reviewing the private offer and we have two open questions that affect our finance team and our reseller (CloudResell):

1) When we accept the AWS private offer, which organization issues the marketplace credits if we need an invoice-level credit (e.g., retroactive adjustment for usage overage)? Is that Amazon, Redwood, or CloudResell?

2) Our reseller requires clarity on how the channel margin is calculated and where the margin is applied (list price vs. net-of-credits). We need this spelled out for our contract and for our reseller onboarding.

Can you confirm the flow and whether Redwood can issue a consolidated credit to Acme if CloudResell is the billing intermediary?

Attached is the PO worksheet we referenced.

Hi Team —

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front: Redwood can coordinate consolidated credits to Acme for platform-level adjustments, but the technical crediting (marketplace invoice adjustments) often originates from AWS. We typically implement a two-step process so accounting and reseller margins remain reconciled:

- Step A: AWS posts the marketplace invoice and any marketplace-level credits (AWS-origin). Those will show on the AWS invoice we reference in the private-offer flow.
- Step B: Redwood issues a balancing credit (if required) to Acme for any product-level adjustments we agreed to (e.g., usage rebate, onboarding credit). This makes the net economics match the private-offer intent.

On reseller margin: margin is computed off the effective net revenue to Redwood after marketplace fees but before Redwood-issued credits. If we issue a Redwood balancing credit back to Acme after the reseller has been paid, we run an internal reconciliation so CloudResell's margin is preserved per the agreed pass-through rules (we either claw or top-up via a separate settlement).

I've attached a simple flowchart that maps who invoices whom and where a credit would appear. Please review and let me know if Acme legal needs this as language for the SOW/Exhibit.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben / Marcus: confirm ops feasibility for issuing a Redwood balancing credit and the likely timing SLA (T+30/T+60).
- Acme: confirm whether CloudResell will remain the billing entity for the initial 12 months.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference

Folks — quick operational notes from the finance/partner side:

1) AWS-origin credits: AWS only adjusts their invoice; they will credit the billed amount to the account on the AWS invoice. For our reconciliation we consume the AWS invoice and reflect the same in Redwood billing reconciliation.

2) Redwood balancing credit: we can issue a Redwood credit note to Acme to reflect any agreed product-level concessions. That credit note is separate from AWS's marketplace credit and will appear on Redwood's statement.

3) Reseller margin treatment: for pass-through resellers like CloudResell we have two standard patterns:
   - Reseller-paid model: reseller invoices Acme at list price; Redwood invoices reseller net and pays them a commission. Any Redwood balancing credit will be reflected in Redwood -> reseller settlements (i.e., we adjust future commission run or issue a settlement).
   - Reseller-contracted model: Redwood lists the private offer in marketplace PSC and the reseller is effectively a channel referrer. The marketplace credits are applied at AWS level; Redwood will make individual settlements with reseller to materially preserve their agreed margin if credits/rebates change economics.

Operational limits & timescales: we can generate Redwood credit notes within 30 business days of an agreed reconciliation event, but if the adjustment requires AWS invoice edits it often depends on AWS support lead times (could be 4–8 weeks).

I copied the AWS rep to ensure they confirm their side for invoice edits. Marcus, can you confirm whether our settlement engine supports a negative settlement line (claw) vs. top-up? If not, we'll need to route this through manual finance batch.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Cloud Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick confirmation from ops/finance:

- Our settlement engine supports both approaches Ben outlined, but negative settlement (clawback) requires a verified audit trail; we prefer to issue a counter-settlement (top-up) to preserve reseller cashflow unless the reseller agrees to remit the claw.
- We can commit to producing Redwood credit notes within 30 business days after the reconciliation trigger. If AWS needs to edit an invoice, that will likely extend the timeline and we'll track in a shared Jira (I created SUP-9882 and linked it to the deal).

Action items:
- Acme: confirm billing entity (CloudResell vs. Acme direct) — Acme reply will determine whether we route credits via reseller settlements or direct Redwood credit notes.
- CloudResell: if you prefer to preserve margin without a delayed settlement, confirm whether you accept a Redwood top-up vs. participating in a clawback.
- Ben / Irene: I'll draft the short SOW exhibit language for the invoice/credit flow and share for legal review by EOD Friday.

Marcus Lin
